public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 143

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/143](https://www.erdosproblems.com/143)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Finset
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos143

/--
Let $A \subseteq (1, \infty)$ be a countably infinite set such that for all $x\neq y\in A$ and
integers $k \geq 1$ we have $|kx - y| \geq 1$.
-/
def WellSeparatedSet (A : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  (A ⊆ (Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ))) ∧ Set.Infinite A ∧ Set.Countable A ∧
  (∀ x ∈ A, ∀ y ∈ A, x ≠ y → (∀ k ≥ (1 : ℕ), 1 ≤ |k * x - y|))

/--
Does this imply that
$$
\liminf \frac{|A \cap [1,x]|}{x} = 0?
$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_143.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℝ), WellSeparatedSet A →
    liminf (fun x => (A ∩ (Set.Icc 1 x)).ncard / x) atTop = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
Or
$$
\sum_{x \in A} \frac{1}{x \log x} < \infty,
$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_143.parts.ii (A : Set ℝ) (h : WellSeparatedSet A) :
    Summable fun (x : A) ↦ 1 / (x * Real.log x) := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): add the two other conjectures.
/-
$$
\sum_{\substack{x < n \\ x \in A}} \frac{1}{x} = o(\log n)?
$$

Perhaps even

$$
\sum_{\substack{x < n \\ x \in A}} \frac{1}{x} \ll \frac{\log x}{\sqrt{\log \log x}}?
$$
-/

end Erdos143

status_issues.source_status: Solved affirmatively as a consequence of Koukoulopoulos–Lamzouri–Lichtman (2025), arXiv:2502.09539, Theorem 1. The stronger convergence question in part (ii) remains open.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/143 credits Koukoulopoulos, Lamzouri, and Lichtman with proving ∑_{a∈A, a<n} 1/a = o(log n) under the stated separation hypothesis. Their paper explicitly treats positive lower natural density as a stronger hypothesis than positive upper logarithmic density. To see the consequence directly, write N_A(t)=|A∩[1,t]|. If liminf N_A(t)/t>0, then N_A(t)≥ct eventually for some c>0; partial summation gives ∑_{a≤x}1/a = N_A(x)/x + ∫₁ˣ N_A(t)/t² dt ≥ c log x + O(1), contradicting their result. Thus part (i) is settled even though the overall problem page remains OPEN.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change part (i) to @[category research solved], replace answer(sorry) with answer(True), and cite KLL25. Keep part (ii) tagged research open.

review.notes: All three declarations are mathematically faithful. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, sorry-free proofs verify that the real prime set satisfies WellSeparatedSet, bounded intersections are finite, their ncard is at most the natural floor of the endpoint, and the density quotient is eventually in [0,1]. Thus neither ncard nor real liminf introduces a default-value defect. The summands are strictly positive, and a proved equivalence with bounded finite subsums confirms the Summable formulation. Boundary proofs and computable rational separation tests also passed. The TODO's little-o bound is now the cited KLL25 result, but has no Lean declaration here.
